scope: Focused review of implemented arXiv full-text completeness and fetch-origin boundaries. Existing GitHub pagination/missing-field/retry classification findings were not repeated.

source_snapshot.state: Dirty worktree under active implementation; the tested source snapshot is identified by the copied-file hashes, not by HEAD alone.
source_snapshot.snapshot_method: Read each source file as bytes, hash exactly those bytes, copy into one temporary standalone Go package, then execute the probe against those copies. No live product files modified.

execution.observation_provenance: Transcript-derived observations from functions.exec result chunk e33eaa. No original stdout/stderr artifact was retained, and no reconstructed file is presented as raw execution output.
execution.environment: Only two httptest HTTP servers on loopback; no external HTTP or browser/provider calls.
execution.cleanup: Temporary standalone package and local servers cleaned after execution. No rerun performed while persisting this review.

findings.title: An invalid PDF fragment is marked as complete full text

input.metadata: A matching arXiv Atom entry for 2304.03442v2, valid publication/update times and one author.
input.response: HTTP 200; Content-Type application/pdf; chunked after explicit Flush(), no Content-Length.
input.structural_condition: No PDF objects, cross-reference/trailer or EOF; body is a header plus repeated plain text.

findings.mechanism: The reviewed adapter accepts length >=1024 and a %PDF- prefix; it does not establish PDF structural completeness. Absent Content-Length does not block Complete.
findings.expected: Invalid/truncated full-text bytes must not be promoted to a complete full-text item.

findings.title: Redirect fetches an unconfigured origin while retaining the trusted canonical label

input.configured_origin: httptest origin A supplied as APIURL and PDFBaseURL
input.redirect: The PDF route returns HTTP 302 to origin B /unexpected-origin, a distinct loopback port not included in the adapter configuration.
input.target_response: Origin B returns the same 2309-byte fragment as the first subtest.

findings.mechanism: The supplied ordinary http.Client follows redirects; adapter does not enforce a configured origin boundary on the actual request chain. Item canonical URL is synthesized from requested arXiv ID and does not identify the response origin.
findings.expected: Validate or deny redirect destinations before an unauthorized origin is fetched; a synthesized canonical URL cannot stand in for authorized fetch provenance.
findings.isolation_note: foreign_hits=1 proves the origin crossing independently of PDF parsing. After PDF validation is repaired, Complete may become false while the redirect defect still exists; assert foreign_hits==0 or an explicitly authorized destination, not merely Complete==false.

probe.content: Exact Go probe source used in the observed run. No raw-output reconstruction.
reproduction_steps: Create an isolated temporary directory outside the product source tree.
Copy sources.go, arxiv.go and github.go from the adapter snapshot being reviewed; record their hashes. The original bytes are identified above but not embedded in this review record.
Copy this probe into the temporary directory as verifier_test.go.
Create go.mod containing module researchos-verifier-source-probe, a blank line, and go 1.27.1.
Run the pinned Go executable with test -run ^TestVerifierArxivPartialAndRedirect$ -count=1 -v . from that directory.

For independent regression checks, assess redirect_false complete/items and redirect_true foreign_hits separately. The original test intentionally failed both on the reviewed snapshot; it does not independently fail solely on foreign_hits.
Retain new raw output and hashes as new verification evidence, then clean the temporary directory.

limits: Early review only; no W07 acceptance or A05 live-source PASS.
Both failures were shown against copied dirty-worktree source, not a release build or actual arXiv service.
No product source, contract, ledger or previous receipt was modified.
Do not treat a future passing original combined probe as sufficient origin-boundary proof without checking foreign_hits independently.
